newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Post half year profit falls to NZ$22.2 million.
newsitem.headline: NZ Post half year profit falls to NZ$22.2 million.

text.p: State-owned New Zealand Post said on Friday its half year profit of $22.2 million, down from $37.6 million, was in line with forecasts.
Revenues for the half year to September 30 increased 3.1 percent to $334.1 million while expenditure rose 12.9 percent to $301.9 million.

The government will receive an interim dividend of $13.3 million on December 16 following payment of a special dividend of $30 million on July 1, 1996 after a directors' review of NZ Post's capital structure.
In the last financial year NZ Post paid a special dividend of $15 million related to the sale of the Auckland post office and another of $25 million, which was a capital reduction.
"New Zealand Post has had two years of record profits, and we have taken the opportunity this year to make some substantial investments in the future of the business," chairman Ross Armstrong said.
"This result is in line with our business plan and our progress this year continues to represent a very good level of return for our shareholders."
The lower result partly reflected the lowering of the standard price of a letter to 40 cents from 45 in October 1995.
One-off costs included lump sum payments from recently agreed collective employment contracts.
NZ Post in its annual report revealed that it had one employee on a salary of $420,000-$430,000 and four more between $250,000-$270,000.
